That came later. Davis Fogle stepped to the line with 12 seconds left and the chance to give the Bulldogs a 3-point lead. After missing the first, his second rimmed out and fell in to the hands of Saliou Niang. As LSU dribbled down the court, they were down 80-78 and needed just a 2 to try and force overtime. Dent had different plans. He dribbled the clock down, stepped back, and BANG. Nothing but net, Tigers lead 81-80 with just 1.5 seconds left on the clock. He did just that and Gonzaga’s lead was down to just 79-78 with a minute to play, leading to a timeout. item.title: Harrison shocks Nunes on UFC return to retain title
item.description: Kayla Harrison has won 20 of her 21 professional fights [Getty Images] Kayla Harrison shocked returning great Amanda Nunes by submitting the former double champion to retain her bantamweight title at UFC 334 in New York. Nunes, 38, was fighting for the first time since she brought her glittering career to a close in 2023, after dominating at bantamweight and featherweight for years. Enticed by the challenge of fighting Harrison, the Brazilian came out of retirement for the bout but could not topple her friend and former training partner. Just 10 months after neck and spinal surgery, 36-year-old American Harrison ended the contest in the fourth round at Madison Square Garden with a rear-naked choke. Afterwards, Harrison reflected on the challenges she's overcome during her career. As a youngster, Harrison was sexually abused by her judo coach, who was sentenced to 10 years in prison after being found guilty. Harrison went on to become a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo before moving into mixed martial arts where she became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion and then won UFC bantamweight gold in just her third fight in the organisation. "I was sexually abused at a young age, statistically I'm not supposed to be here," said Harrison. "If you'd told me at six years old this would be my life and at 16, I wouldn't have believed you. "I'm really grateful, humbled and it's an honour and privilege to stand before you." In the main event, heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Josh Hokit. In a gruelling contest which featured a record 383 significant strikes in a UFC heavyweight bout, Frenchman Gane's counter striking off the back foot proved the difference. Harrison cements status as all-time great Harrison submitted Nunes with a rear-naked choke [Getty Images] Nunes left the UFC in 2023 as the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts. During Nunes' remarkable run, she beat some of the greatest names in MMA history, such as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Valentina Shevchenko, but it was the prospect of fighting Harrison which brought her out of retirement. The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, which Nunes left in 2022. Nunes started well and stung Harrison with a number of straight rights, but found herself in trouble at the end of the round with the American in a dominant position on the ground. Despite appearing to have an advantage on the feet, Nunes continued to try and grapple but it was a tactic which played into Harrison's hands. Harrison took the fight to the floor with a powerful hip toss, before later cutting Nunes with a big elbow and right hand on the ground. The decisive moment came in the fourth round as Harrison caught a kick before throwing Nunes off-balance and locking in the fight-ending submission. item.title: Rice hits back at Baena's claims that Yamal deserved Ballon d'Or over Kane
item.description: Rice hits back at Baena's claims that Yamal deserved Ballon d'Or over Kane Ahead of Spain's meeting with England, Declan Rice has hit back at Alex Baena's suggestion that Lamine Yamal deserved the Ballon d'Or over Harry Kane. When asked if the game is a great opportunity for Kane to show the world that he was the one who truly deserved that award, Rice believes the Bayern Munich star can do exactly that. “I think in Harry's case, for me and for everyone in England, Harry deserved the Ballon d'Or," the English midfielder said during the Three Lions' press conference. "I think if you look at his season, his numbers, the trophies he won and the way he performed in those games, it wasn't just about goals. "He delivered man-of-the-match performances. He was relentless. So, I can understand why every Spanish player is obviously going to say Lamine. "Lamine is an incredible player, one of the best players in the world, and he's going to win plenty of Ballon d'Or's in the future. “But I think this time it was right that Harry won, and I think he fully deserved it,” Rice concluded ahead of their meeting with the 2026 World Cup winners in Madrid.

item.title: Key Stats that defined Penn State’s blowout victory over Minnesota
item.description: Penn State head coach Matt Campbell has done an excellent job of getting his team back on track. The blue and white were on a brutal four-game losing streak that took the air out of the season, but Campbell has responded with an impressive three-game winning streak. The defense has been excellent this entire year, with the exception of a couple of games in early October against Northwestern and USC , and now the offense is finally catching up to them. They had another good performance on Saturday against Minnesota, marking the first time since conference play began that the offense put together back-to-back solid showings. Let’s look at a few stats on both sides of the ball that show how Penn State pulled off this dominant 42-14 win . Rushing yards Running back Carson Hansen had the best game of his Penn State career last week against Washington . Well, he immediately outdid himself this week against Minnesota , going for 126 yards and a touchdown. The most impressive part of Hansen’s day is he got all of his production in the first half. He came up hobbled at the end of the second quarter and never returned, so hopefully it was just a precautionary measure since the team was winning 21-0 when he exited. Third-down conversions The Nittany Lions went into Saturday’s game as one of the best third-down defenses in the entire nation, and they certainly lived up to the billing. Minnesota was just 3-for-13 on third downs, and it was even wors in the first half when the offense was 1-for-7. The futility on money downs made it impossible for the offense to gain a rhythm. The unit was disjointed and inefficient the entire night, and it was largely because of Penn State’s exceptionality on third down. Drives starting in opponent’s territory This is a fairly unconventional stat, but it was one of the biggest reasons for the blue and white’s dominant win. They had three drives start in Minnesota’s territory, and they scored touchdowns on each of them. Conversely, the Golden Gophers never started a drive on Penn State’s end of the field. The Nittany Lions just continue to find unique advantages to win games. They possessed the ball for nearly 75% of game time against Purdue, and this week they had uncommonly favorable field position. You know what they say — good teams find ways to win games. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . item.title: Former Lyon and Napoli manager Rudi Garcia admits he came close to landing Manchester United job five years before Mauricio Pochettino's arrival
item.description: FBL-WC-2026-MATCH98-ESP-BEL - AFP Former Lyon and Napoli head coach Rudi Garcia has revealed he held two separate interviews for the Manchester United managerial post back in 2021. The Frenchman was considered for the Old Trafford hotseat five years prior to the club's latest appointment of Mauricio Pochettino. Frenchman recalls interim dugout shortlist Garcia emerged as a candidate to replace Ole Gunnar Solskjaer when the Norwegian's three-year reign ended following a heavy 4-1 Premier League defeat at Watford. Because that dismissal occurred midway through the 2021-22 campaign, the Red Devils hierarchy decided to bring in a temporary boss until the summer. The 62-year-old was available having left Lyon at the end of the previous season following nearly two years in charge. Two interviews precede Rangnick appointment Having previously won a Ligue 1 and Coupe de France double with Lille in 2011, the experienced tactician believed he had a strong case to take the reins in England. However, Old Trafford chiefs ultimately overlooked him and appointed Rangnick on a short-term contract in December 2021. Recalling how close he came to landing the role, Garcia told The Athletic : "Yes, I interviewed twice to work in this fantastic club, one of the best clubs in the world. "I'd like to work in England and I met Darren Fletcher and John Murtough. It was an interim role and they asked me what I would do once it was over. I told them I would do so well that I would be staying in Manchester, but they gave the job to Ralf." Four permanent bosses follow departure Rangnick went on to oversee a sixth-place top-flight finish during his brief spell before Erik ten Hag arrived in the summer of 2022 as the first of four permanent appointments in just over four years. The Dutchman was eventually succeeded by Ruben Amorim in November 2024, prior to former midfielder Michael Carrick taking charge earlier this year . Following Carrick's sacking on Thursday, the club have now turned to former Tottenham Hotspur manager Pochettino to steady the ship. The Argentine will officially begin work this coming Thursday having penned a contract that runs until the summer of 2029. Mixed spells define subsequent career Meanwhile, Garcia returned to management with Al-Nassr, where he signed Cristiano Ronaldo following the forward's Old Trafford exit before being dismissed in April 2023 less than a season into his reign. He took over at Napoli three months later only to be sacked 12 games into the 2023-24 Serie A campaign. Most recently, he guided Belgium to this summer's World Cup quarter-finals before departing once eventual champions Spain eliminated them.

item.title: Surya blazes back in style, 21-ball 60 powers Mumbai to emphatic win over Hyderabad
item.description: Suryakumar Yadav could hardly have scripted a better response after what he recently described as a couple of "difficult months" following his omission from the Indian team despite captaining the country to the 2026 T20 World Cup title. Leading Mumbai in their Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy opener against Hyderabad at Kolkata's Jadavpur University Ground on Saturday, the former India T20 skipper smashed an unbeaten 60 off just 21 balls, bringing up his half-century in a mere 15 deliveries. The 36-year-old hammered six fours and five sixes at a strike rate of 285.71 as Mumbai chased down 173 in just 13.1 overs, winning by seven wickets with 41 balls to spare. Batting at No. 4, Suryakumar tore into the Hyderabad attack from the outset and shared a 65-run stand off only 23 balls with Musheer Khan, who blasted 51 off 24 balls. Sooryavanshi disappoints on captaincy debut Teen batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi added another chapter to his remarkable rise by becoming the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history. At 15 years and 232 days, the Bihar prodigy surpassed Croatia's Zach Vukusic, who captained his national side at 17 years and 311 days in 2025. The youngster, entrusted with Bihar's leadership for the opening phase of the tournament, endured a disappointing outing on the field. He made 18 off 12 balls as Bihar, who scored 137 for nine, went down to Saurashtra by five wickets. Mayank's 5 wkts help Delhi win Pacer Mayank Yadav ripped through Jammu & Kashmir with figures of five for 14 in three overs to power Delhi to a commanding 103-run victory in Indore. Delhi piled up 243 for six, powered by Himmat Singh's 63 off 26 balls and Priyansh Arya's 58 off 29, before Mayank's pace proved too hot to handle. Karnataka prevail Pacers Abhilash Shetty (4-26) and Vijaykumar Vyshak (3-28) shared seven wickets as Karnataka restricted Bengal to 165 for nine and sealed a 19-run victory at the Wankhede Stadium.

item.title: Barcelona receive €100 million offer for La Masia star amid Chelsea, Manchester United interest
item.description: Barcelona receive €100 million offer for La Masia star amid Chelsea, Manchester United interest Even in a season where Lamine Yamal and Raphinha have attracted the limelight once again through their exceptional performances, Fermin Lopez has proven why he is such an important part of Barcelona. The Spanish international has quietly emerged as one of Barcelona’s most productive players with eight goals and seven assists in all competitions. Fermin’s brilliant season has not gone unnoticed either, with a number of Premier League clubs keen on signing the playmaker. Barcelona receive €100 million offer for Fermin Fermin has transformed into a genuine star at Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) According to Diario SPORT , a host of Premier League clubs who were keen on Fermin last summer have revisited their interest in the player. In fact, Barcelona have even received an offer of around €100 million for the services of the Spanish international. Chelsea, in particular, had tabled a bid of around €70 million last summer. But it is likely that the Blues, along with other Premier League clubs such as Manchester United have tabled a bid higher than that. Chelsea and Man United are apparently the teams who have shown the most concrete interest in signing Fermin. Fermin has no desire to leave Fermin Lopez wants to remain at Barcelona. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) However, Barcelona are not worried about the prospect of Fermin Lopez leaving the club anytime shown. The player has shown no desire to leave Barcelona, even though he is a distant third behind Yamal and Raphinha, as far as the team’s biggest attacking stars are concerned. Fermin has a contract at Camp Nou until 2031, which gives the Blaugrana significant leverage even when a Premier League team does make a push to sign the player. Barcelona are also aware of Fermin’s progress and are expected to soon sit down with the player’s representative over a new contract that will likely come with a significant raise in salary. In any case, Fermin has turned deaf ears to interest from these Premier League clubs and will not consider an exit from Barcelona, no matter how lucrative an offer he gets.

item.title: Peter Shilton reacts to Harry Kane becoming England’s most-capped player
item.description: Photo by Carl Recine - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images | UEFA via Getty Images Peter Shilton held the record for most caps by an England player in history, earning 125 between 1970 and 1990. Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane broke that record when he made his 126th appearance in Wembley Stadium against Croatia in the UEFA Nations League, and Shilton says Kane and only Kane deserved to break his record. “I’ve held the record for quite a few years now, but if anyone deserves to overtake me, it’s Harry,” Shilton said (via FIFA as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). “I couldn’t think of anyone better. He’s been an incredible servant and leader for so long now, and has scored plenty of goals along the way. I think I will be going on to the pitch to present him with something.” Kane presented his Ballon d’Or before a magnificent tifo honoring his success prior to kickoff and earned his side the win by converting a penalty for a 2-1 win. item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 28: Ronald Araujo of Liverpool during the Carabao Cup Fourth Round match between Liverpool and Chelsea at Anfield on October 28, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images Barcelona had a busy summer transfer window that saw plenty of ins and outs as Hansi Flick reshaped his squad for the 2026-27 campaign. Some big names left the club on loan and have endured mixed fortunes in the first few months of the new campaign. With domestic football currently on pause due to the international break, let’s take a look at how they have all been getting on. Ronald Araujo Uruguayan defender Ronald Araujo agreed a season-long loan with Liverpool and has been a huge hit in the Premier League with the Reds so far this season. The defender was in need of a fresh start after a tough time at Barcelona and has found his form, his smile and a whole lot of love in England at Anfield. Araujo has become a regular at right-back for Andoni Iraola’s side and seems to be thriving on the Premier League’s physicality and intensity. The center-back has also scored twice and already has Liverpool fans asking the club to sign him up . There is reportedly a buy option in his loan deal, although Araujo has insisted it’s too early to talk about the future. What is certain is that the loan has been a great success so far for all concerned. There’s still a long way to go between now and the end of the campaign but Araujo looks rejuvenated in the red shirt of Liverpool. Marc Casado Marc Casado reluctantly left Barcelona in the summer, leaving it until the last minute to seal a temporary move to Deportivo in a bid for regular minutes. The arrival of Rodri in the summer saw Casado slip even further down the pecking order at Barcelona and he chose Deportivo after admitting he was impressed by the club on a previous visit with the Catalans. Unfortunately for Casado, all has not gone smoothly so far. The midfielder made four appearances and was then sidelined with a fractured collarbone that required surgery. The Barcelona loanee was expected to miss three months but managed to return at the start of November against Espanyol. Now fully fit, he will be hoping to make an impact after an injury-interrupted start to life in A Coruna. Marc-Andre ter Stegen Goalkeeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen signed for Ajax in the summer , a direct request from manager Michel, and has been enjoying regular football after a difficult time with injuries. The stopper is the club’s No. 1 and has also been installed as Jurgen Klopp’s first choice goalkeeper with the Germany national squad. Ajax currently sit in third place in the table, just one point off top spot, and Ter Stegen has done a solid job. item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 14: (R-L) Ciryl Gane of France punches Josh Hokit in their heavyweight championship fight during the UFC 334 event at Madison Square Garden on November 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Last night (Sat., Nov. 14, 2026), Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) ventured forth to Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York for UFC 334 . Twin title fights topped the promotion’s return to MSG, making for an exciting and high-profile night of action. In the main event, Ciryl Gane aimed for the first defense of his newly-minted Heavyweight crown opposite divisional upstart Josh Hokit . In addition, Amanda Nunes returned after nearly three years on the sidelines in an attempt to recapture her Bantamweight crown from Judo Olympian Kayla Harrison . The rest of the card was stacked with fun matchups and interesting talent, so let’s get right to the best performances and highlight finishes of the evening: A Record-Setting Heavyweight War Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit was an outstanding scrap, the best Heavyweight fight in quite some time. Gane started strong. Hokit wrestled right away and surged forward relentlessly, forcing Gane onto the back foot immediately. From his bike, Gane was nevertheless able to snap Hokit’s chin back repeatedly. It didn’t deter Hokit and his fastball of a right hand, but those jabs were the most significant punches of the opening frame. In addition, Gane did well to start punching the body early in the fight. Gane was operating without kicks, however, in fear of the takedown, and he was sprinting all over the cage. As a result, he started breathing more heavily in the second, and Hokit was able to close the gap more often. By the third, Hokit was dictating the pace and landing the better shots. Not only did he connect with the right hand, but he started stomping on Gane’s foot like he was trying to put out a fire, and he also scored some knifing elbows from the clinch. In round four, Gane made a decision that changed the entire fight. After running around for 15 straight minutes, Gane began to stand his ground and put more weight into his strikes. In addition, Gane had avoided throwing kicks and knees for much of the fight in fear of the takedown. Since Hokit hadn’t managed to do much with his wrestling in the first three rounds, Gane was able to more effectively open up with his other weapons and take that risk. item.title: “Jessica Pegula Did Mirra Andreeva A Favor” – Serena Williams’ Coach Explains How WTA Finals Controversy Became A ‘Catalyst’ For Teenager
item.description: Mirra Andreeva © Imagn Serena Williams’ coach Rennae Stubbs believes Mirra Andreeva’s remarkable run at the 2026 WTA Finals stems from controversial comments Jessica Pegula made about her ahead of the year-end championships. Andreeva, making her WTA Finals debut this year, has reached the final after three dominant Round Robin phase wins. The 19-year-old then defeated Pegula in another impressive semifinal. During a practice session in the tournament buildup that was streamed live, a courtside microphone picked up Pegula brazenly criticizing Andreeva’s mentality. The American veteran called the young Russian a ‘diva’ and said that if Andreeva improves her attitude, she will go on to achieve even greater things. Andreeva, despite her tender age, already has six senior singles titles, including this year’s Roland Garros crown. After the 19-year-old’s 6-3, 6-4 win over Pegula in the semis, Stubbs took to X and wrote: “I think @JPegula did Mirra a favor by making those comments last week. It was a wake up call by a peer & it may have just been the catalyst to make her the best player in the world!! 😂 … because she has been very Un-diva like this week! Head down, great attitude & crushing!!” Mirra Andreeva’s victory over Jessica Pegula at WTA Finals 2026 ensures World No. 2 spot for the youngster Andreeva will replace Aryna Sabalenka as the new World No. 2 once the new rankings are published after the WTA Finals conclude. Interestingly, in the Round Robin phase, Andreeva and Sabalenka had locked horns, and the youngster came away with a deserving 6-4, 6-0 win over the former No. 1. Elina Svitolina of Ukraine awaits Andreeva in the final , and the 19-year-old should be confident going into the match. The youngster clashed with the veteran and former WTA Finals champion in their opening Round Robin match. Andreeva won by the same score she recorded against Sabalenka. Andreeva is also the youngest player since the iconic Maria Sharapova to reach the WTA Finals’ championship match. In 2004, Sharapova not only reached the last hurdle, but also conquered it by defeating the legendary Serena Williams in three sets. item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 14: Kayla Harrison reacts after her submission victory over Amanda Nunes of Brazil in their women's bantamweight championship fight during the UFC 334 event at Madison Square Garden on November 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Zuffa LLC) Kayla Harrison has emerged from her UFC 334 fight against WMMA GOAT Amanda Nunes battered but victorious … so now what? Harrison has been on her own quest to cement her place in WMMA history as one of the best, but has had the bad luck of coming into the UFC after many of the best women in her division have left. Ronda Rousey had retired, Amanda Nunes had retired, Cris Cyborg was deemed a pain in the ass and released into the wild. So up until Saturday night, Kayla’s best win was over an aged Holly Holm in 2024. Now she has a hard fought win over Amanda Nunes to hang her hat on. Nunes looked as deadly as ever in her first fight in three years, but her insistence on trying to grapple with the two-time Olympic gold medal judoka cost her the first three rounds of the fight and then got her finished in the fourth (watch the highlights here). She’d batter Harrison early, only to give up on striking and end up on the ground fighting for her life. Harrison made her pay every time she’d clinch up and tapped her the second she left her neck exposed, but it really feels like Nunes earned the loss over Harrison earning the win. The W next to her name at UFC 334 will only look better as time goes on. Given how much she suffers to make 135, why continue? There’s certainly not a whole lot of good options for her to fight. Let’s go through the options: Nunes’ performance at UFC 334 isn’t going to create a lot of demand for a rematch at featherweight. Ronda Rousey is retired again and made how much she hates the current UFC leadership a cornerstone of her comeback fight earlier this year. And UFC CEO Dana White described ‘steroid-user’ Cris Cyborg as ‘a nightmare to deal with’ back in 2019 when he released her from her contract. Even the only woman to ever beat Harrison, Larissa Pacheco, isn’t a likely option. After finishing her contract with PFL at the end of 2025, Pacheco reached out to UFC matchmakers. “I am not interested but thank you,” is the text response she got from Mick Maynard. The red-hot Australian winning machine blew New Zealand away in the first half as they cantered to a record fourth World Cup title - and fourth in a row - with a 34-10 win in Brisbane. Making light work of the blistering conditions, which necessitated a drinks break in either half and an extended interval, the Jillaroos ran in six tries to the Kiwi Ferns' one in the opening 35 minutes, including an initial burst of 24 unanswered points and a hat-trick for Chapman. Record books were consulted at the break, with Australia on course to challenge New Zealand's 58-0 winning margin from the 2003 final. But the two sides neutralised one another during the second period, New Zealand maintaining their record of not conceding after the break at this tournament - and bagging a consolation try - albeit with Australia long out of sight. The undisputed dominant force in women's rugby league, Australia are now unbeaten in 16 World Cup matches - a run stretching back to July 2013. Aside from a brief first-half scare against Fiji in the semi-finals, who became the first side for 13 years to open the scoring in a World Cup game against Australia, it has been a serene procession to the title, scoring 306 points while conceding just 30. item.description: Aryna Sabalenka will be replaced as world number two by Mirra Andreeva on Monday [Getty Images] Aryna Sabalenka has apologised and denied claims that she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian. A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday. Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended." Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her "all the best for the rest of the tournament". Svitolina races into WTA Finals showpiece against Andreeva I hope matches between us are respected - Svitolina Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country. They also do not take pre-match photographs with each other. But Svitolina, who says she has seen the viral clips of Sabalenka's outburst on social media, says she hopes the matches between the two can be "respected". In response to Sabalenka's statement, Svitolina said on Saturday: "As we see there's many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags and of course they want me to win this particular match. "We've played many times with Aryna. She has her fans. I have my fans. "I just hope the matches between us [are] respected. item.description: Real Madrid academy sensation outshines Guler and Bellingham with remarkable assist record Real Madrid continue to have talented players coming through their academy who look destined for greatness in the future. While not all these players may get a chance in the first team, the club often makes a good profit from selling them . This helps them strengthen the first team by bringing in players like Carlos Espi, who is already making an impression despite limited opportunities. Coincidentally, another youngster with a similar nickname has been quietly making waves at Valdebebas. According to MARCA , 18-year-old left-back Jose Luis Saez Espinosa, better known as ‘Espi’, has emerged as the leading assist provider across Madrid’s four highest-ranked teams. Espi leads Real Madrid’s assist charts The youngster has registered six assists in just ten appearances for Juvenil A this season, an impressive return considering his defensive position. Interestingly, his tally exceeds those of several established first-team stars, including Arda Guler with five, Jude Bellingham with four and Kylian Mbappe with three. The Real Madrid academy continues to produce gems. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) He also leads the academy rankings, ahead of Juvenil A team-mate Company, who has five assists, and Castilla midfielder Leiva, who has two. However, Espi is about more than just his attacking contributions. The teenager has established himself as an important member of Alvaro Lopez’s defensive set-up. His development has now earned him a place in Real Madrid C’s squad for Sunday’s encounter against San Sebastian de los Reyes. Real Madrid youngster attracting attention from higher levels It is very clear that Espi is considered one of the biggest talents coming through Castilla at the moment. The defender was previously included in Castilla’s squad against Alcorcon in September and has attracted attention from coaches Julian Lopez de Lerma and Marc Carrasco. Espinosa’s rapid growth has been likened to Espi. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) It is still early days, but Espinosa will know that if he continues to develop at a similar rate, it won’t be long before Jose Mourinho starts to take notice. The Portuguese manager will want young players who are determined to prove themselves at the highest level. Left-back had been a problem position for the first team until this past summer, when the club signed Marc Cucurella. Espi could look to provide competition for the Spaniard at some point in the future, and it remains to be seen how his evolution pans out.

item.title: Barcelona midfielder’s injury could be more serious than thought – report
item.description: Barcelona midfielder’s injury could be more serious than thought – report Barcelona have been dealt an early blow during the international break, in the form of Frenkie de Jong. The Dutch midfielder, recovering from an injury not too long ago, picked up discomfort during the Netherlands’ victory over Greece. The Dutch FA was quick to announce that the midfielder has been ruled out for the next game, with Xavi Hernandez assuring the media that it was only a minor knock. It was reported that the decision to send him back to Barcelona was only precautionary. Bigger worry over de Jong’s injury De Jong has recently recovered from a long injury layoff. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) However, a recent report from Diario AS has indicated that de Jong’s injury could be more serious than thought. It appears de Jong did not simply pick up discomfort in his back. The area he felt most pain after the game was in his pubis. This makes things a lot more complicated, as cases of Lamine Yamal and Nico Williams have shown that pubalgia-related injuries can be complex and take a while to heal. The report speculates that the fact that the Dutch FA was so quick to put out a statement over de Jong’s fitness could be a sign of something more serious. What’s next for de Jong? Important few days ahead for de Jong. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) If it is indeed a pubis-related issue, then Barcelona must be very careful and monitor the player’s recovery before taking a call on his fitness. The report adds that de Jong is set to be examined by Barcelona’s medical team on Monday, after which the extent of the problem will be diagnosed. The next few days, therefore, are going to be critical not only for de Jong but for Barcelona as well. The Dutchman’s return to fitness, after all, seemed like a boon after a long period on the sidelines, and even more so with Rodri currently out with an injury as well. Barcelona will hope the problem is not pubis-related and that it was indeed a back discomfort, so that the midfielder can be ready to feature in the club’s next game against Villarreal.

item.title: ‘Mike Tomlin Is Not Coaching Again’ — NFL Fans React As Steelers Legend Says Mason Rudolph ‘Had a Punchable Face’
item.description: ‘Mike Tomlin Is Not Coaching Again,’ ‘Myles (Garrett) Wasn’t Lying’ — NFL Fans React as Steelers Legend Says Mason Rudolph ‘Had a Punchable Face’ Mike Tomlin isn’t holding back now that he is no longer coaching the Pittsburgh Steelers. During an appearance on Cameron Heyward’s “Not Just Football” podcast, the former coach looked back on the infamous 2019 clash between Myles Garrett and Mason Rudolph and made a bold statement. Tomlin said Rudolph had a “punchable face,” and while he meant it jokingly, the comment quickly caught the attention of NFL fans. Many didn’t find it funny, especially those who remember the incident between Garrett and Rudolph. Mike Tomlin Revisits 2019 Fight Between Myles Garrett and Mason Rudolph The incident happened Nov. 14, 2019, during a “Thursday Night Football” game between the Steelers and the Cleveland Browns. With seconds remaining in Cleveland’s 21-7 win, Garrett and Rudolph got into a heated confrontation after a tackle. It escalated when the defensive end ripped off Rudolph’s helmet and hit him over the head with it, setting off a fight between players from both teams. The NFL suspended Garrett, which cost him the final six games of the 2019 season, and he also received a $45,623 fine and lost about $1.2 million in salary. Nearly seven years later, Tomlin revisited the moment while chatting with Heyward, who reminded the former coach of his earlier comment about Rudolph. “You said Mason (Rudolph) has the most punchable face. I agree with that,” Heyward said. Tomlin didn’t back away from it, responding , “I probably shouldn’t have said that. But was it not true? We love Rudolph. He’s lovable, but he’s punchable. He’s our punchable face. He kind of lightened the mood, though, when I said it, right? I was like, yeah, he does. He is very punchable.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Although Tomlin made it clear that he liked Rudolph, his choice of words quickly became a talking point among NFL fans. “Mike Tomlin is not coaching again,” one fan wrote . Another fan criticized the former coach, writing , “[Expletive] Tomlin – rude!” “What happened to protecting your guy?” another commenter asked , questioning why Tomlin appeared to side with Garrett rather than defend his former quarterback. After missing seven games following knee surgery, Garrett returned in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders and immediately made his presence felt. He recorded three sacks and forced a fumble in the Rams’ 20-13 victory, and he ranked No. 1 in the league that week with a PFN Edge Impact Score of 95.3. item.title: Australia's Sayers 'took sandpaper from field'
item.description: Pat Cummins (left) and Usman Khawaja (right) have given conflicting accounts of the sandpaper scandal from 2018 [Getty Images] Former Australia bowler Chadd Sayers says he helped take sandpaper off the ground in the match before the infamous Cape Town Test and has backed Usman Khawaja's recollection over Pat Cummins' - saying he believes "everyone knew" about the plan to ball tamper. Sayers, 39, was 12th man during the second Test of the 2018 series against South Africa in Gqeberha, previously known as Port Elizabeth, and backed the claim from Khawaja's book that sandpaper was also used there. "It was given to me to take off," Sayers said on SEN Radio. "That wasn't planned or anything. It was a wicket or drinks break after tea." The Sandpapergate Scandal 'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja claims Australia doomed to live with stench of sandpapergate Sayers also said there was a "60 to 90-minute" meeting in the Australia dressing room after Bancroft had been caught using sandpaper in Cape Town, in which players discussed taking collective responsibility - something Khawaja claims but Cummins said he did not remember in his extraordinary news conference on Friday. "I am comfortable sitting here that I believe everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used," said Sayers, whose one Test was the final match of that series. "It [sandpaper] was used in two Test matches and there were discussions in the changing rooms. "I'm not taking sides, it's just my recollection of what took place. "After the occurrence in Cape Town, we all sat in the changing rooms after that day's play and, probably for 60 to 90 minutes, we talked about what had happened and I guess where to next." Sayers took two wickets in the fourth Test in Johannesburg - the Test after Australia's use of sandpaper to aid reverse swing had been uncovered [Getty Images] Sayers first backed Khawaja's recollections last week, saying "everything" in the former opener's book was "accurate". In an episode which has dominated headlines in Australia and elsewhere, Khawaja said the entire Australia team knew about the plan to use sandpaper to tamper with the ball and should have taken responsibility. Cummins, a bowler in that squad and now Australia captain, emphatically rejected the claims by calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense". The bowlers - Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon - have always claimed they did not know. David Warner accused Cricket Australia of a "cover-up" on Saturday, suggesting Hazlewood, Starc and Lyon had not been interviewed as part of the governing body's investigation. Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer praised his team’s defensive performance after the No. 3 Crimson Tide earned a 21-6 win over Vanderbilt at FirstBank Stadium on Saturday. The Commodores failed to score a touchdown as Alabama put together its best defensive showing in terms of points allowed this season. One of the biggest positives for DeBoer was how his defense handled crucial third- and fourth-down situations. Vanderbilt converted just two of its 15 third-down attempts and managed only one conversion on four tries on fourth down. The Crimson Tide also recorded five sacks and nine tackles for loss while limiting the Commodores to just 21 rushing yards on 23 carries. Speaking after the victory, DeBoer pointed out the aggression his defense has displayed in recent weeks , especially during pivotal situations. Third down, fourth down, holding them to field goals that continued to be the case again today. So really like the way they’re flying around. Getting pressure at the right times. It helps when the personnel up front is doing what they are doing. Playing good team football on that side of the ball, for sure.” Vanderbilt managed just six points, the fewest Alabama has surrendered to an opponent this season. It was also the lowest point total by an SEC opponent against the Crimson Tide since Missouri was shut out 34-0 in 2024. Inside linebacker QB Reese played a huge role despite coming off the bench. He led Alabama with eight tackles, including one tackle for loss and a sack. However, the Crimson Tide does have an area to address. The defense failed to force a turnover, allowing the Commodores to finish without a takeaway despite Alabama giving up an interception by quarterback Keelon Russell in the third quarter and a fourth-quarter strip sack.
